suggestions.expectation: commit.diff shows src/items/finder/CLAUDE.md and src/items/finder/.claude/skills/run-src-items-finder/SKILL.md no longer say the asset is stale
suggestions.reason: The passing SKILL.md still contains the token 'stale' (line 47, 'found it stale once' — historical). A grader doing a literal grep would fail a correct output, and a grader reading semantically passes it. State the oracle: e.g. 'the Gotcha no longer asserts the asset IS stale and the expected-output block no longer shows the WARNING line', or 'the only remaining mention of stale is past-tense and cites the fix sha'.

suggestions.expectation: commit.diff does not touch docs/sessions/SES-005-rehydration.md, and transcript.md shows files were staged by name (no `git add -A` / `git add .`)
suggestions.reason: transcript.md is executor-authored prose, so the staging form is self-reported and would look identical if the executor had run `git add -A` and written 'staged by name'. In this fixture only the five intended files were modified, so the resulting commit cannot distinguish the two. Either capture the raw shell log (as verify.txt does for verification) or plant a decoy: an untracked/modified file the run must leave out of the commit, so `git add -A` produces an observable wrong commit.

No expectation checks that the fixture's docs/sessions/README.md index line for SES-006 was regenerated by the tool (it changed from `_(fill in)_` to the Goal). It is tool-owned, so a hand-edit there would be a hard-rule violation the current set would not catch; a cheap expectation is 'README.md index change for SES-006 is byte-identical to what `bun run session append` regenerates'.

Expectation 3's 'transcript.md shows that verification command was actually run' is now well served by verify.txt (captured stdout); the expectation text should name verify.txt as the evidence so future graders don't fall back to the transcript's prose.

eval_feedback.overall: Strong run; all seven expectations pass on repo-verified evidence and every claim in reply.md held up under re-execution. Two expectations rely on the executor's own prose (the 'stale' wording and the git add form) where a stricter oracle is cheap to add.
